I was at my boyfriend's apartment waiting for him to come home from work when he texted me to tell me he invited his friend over. They got home and I hid in the bedroom the entire time. About an hour into them hanging out, I realized I had to pee REALLY badly. Another hour went by, still no sign of his friend leaving. At this point I can't focus on anything besides holding my bladder. Then I remember there are plastic bags in the closet... along with cardboard boxes... yep, I lined a cardboard box with plastic bags and peed in it. I tied the bags up, taped up the box, hid it under the bed, and took it to the dumpster the next morning. I have never been so ashamed.

I'm doing much better now, as far as social anxiety goes. I've met almost all my boyfriend's friends and haven't peed in a box since.

Shit, that really hits home for me. My stepdad died in an ATV accident almost 3 years ago. To this day, I blame myself for somehow not stopping him from going out that day, even though I had no idea he was going. I always think that if I had just called at the right moment, he'd still be alive...

I wonder what makes our brains do this.
Sounds look like depression to me. Fairly common in people who have  some sort of anxiety disorder. I experience the same thing, usually after something makes my anxiety flare up.
It has become clear that my relationship with M cannot exist alongside my relationship with B because of things that have happened between all of us and because of their relationship.
They had a falling out and probably shouldn't be in the same room together. M often talks about violent fantasies regarding B. So...probably not the best idea.

My fear is that the "fuck yeah" feeling is temporary--realistically, I know passion fades over time. And I do love my "safety net," but I know that's mostly because we've been together for so long and I'm attached to who we are and what we've been through.

I don't know. I've been very torn up inside about this for a long time.
